title: A Pre-Modeling Statistical Audit Framework
text: PrismR open-source R statistical engineering package introduces formal concept Model Readiness—rigorous statistical audit verifying whether tabular data genuinely suitable machine learning model trained. modern data science, teams routinely spend weeks fine-tuning hyperparameter grids, selecting gradient boosting architectures, engineering deep networks, suffer models : 1. Silently overfit surrogate IDs target leakage channels. 2. Fail production feature distributions drifted training inference. 3. Underperform mathematically severe skewness extreme kurtosis violate distributional assumptions linear models, neural layers, distance metrics. PrismR eliminates entire class failures establishing Statistical Validation Layer preprocessing model training.
code: Traditional ML Pipeline (Vulnerable): Raw Data ──► Data Cleaning ──► Feature Engineering ──► Model Training                                                         ▲                                                         └── [Silent failures discovered in production]  PrismR Pipeline (Hardened): Raw Data ──► Data Cleaning ──► ┌────────────────────────────────────┐                                │     Statistical Validation Layer   │ ◄── PrismR Gatekeeper                                │   (Quality • Leakage • Transforms  │                                │        • Feature Stability)        │                                └─────────────────┬──────────────────┘                                                  │ [Verdict: Model Ready]                                                  ▼                                Feature Engineering ──► Model Training

title: A Pre-Modeling Statistical Audit Framework
text: Population Stability Index (PSI): PSI=∑=1k(Actuali−Expectedi)×ln⁡(ActualiExpectedi)\text{PSI} = \sum_{=1}^k \left( \text{Actual}_i - \text{Expected}_i \right) \times \ln\left( \frac{\text{Actual}_i}{\text{Expected}_i} \right) Bayesian Laplace Smoothing (α=0.5\alpha = 0.5): Applies pseudo-counts prior probability normalization: Pi=Ni+0.5N+0.5×kP_i = \frac{N_i + 0.5}{N + 0.5 \times k}Guarantees numeric stability, eliminating division--zero errors infinite log penalties bin unobserved one partition. Adaptive Quantile Binning: Bins continuous numeric features equal-frequency quantiles derived baseline distribution. Dual Wasserstein Distance (W1W_1): Computes raw Earth Mover’s Distance well Scale-Normalized Wasserstein: W¯1=W1(P,Q)σpooled\overline{W}_1 = \frac{W_1(P, Q)}{\sigma_{\text{pooled}}}Enables direct comparison drift severity across features differing physical units scales. Categorical Feature Tracking: Bins discrete levels, capturing novel categories appearing evaluation data. Unix Standard (Silence Default): Runs silently (verbose = FALSE), returning structured programmatic lists ideal automated CI/CD pipelines.

title: A Pre-Modeling Statistical Audit Framework
text: PrismR flags issues across multiple modules, order data scientist resolve ? Trying optimize transformations feature leaks target, imputing values column suffers severe temporal drift, wasted engineering effort. PrismR establishes structured 4-Phase Remediation Protocol:
code: [ RAW TABULAR DATA ]                                 │                                 ▼  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │ Phase 1: Data Leakage (`detect_leakage`)                    │ ◄── PRIORITY 1: DROP / ISOLATE  │ Action: Remove ID keys, exact target leakers, proxy vectors │     (Hard Veto Blocker)  └──────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┘                                 │                                 ▼  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │ Phase 2: Data Quality (`quality_score`)                     │ ◄── PRIORITY 2: CLEANSE  │ Action: Deduplicate rows, drop zero-variance constants,     │     (Structural Hygiene)  │         impute or drop heavy-missingness columns            │  └──────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┘                                 │                                 ▼  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │ Phase 3: Feature Stability (`feature_stability`)            │ ◄── PRIORITY 3: STABILIZE  │ Action: Audit covariate shift across time/batches.          │     (Distribution Shift)  │         Resolve drift BEFORE attempting mathematical transforms!  └──────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┘                                 │                                 ▼  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │ Phase 4: Transformations (`recommend_transform`)            │ ◄── PRIORITY 4: OPTIMIZE  │ Action: Apply Box-Cox / Log / Yeo-Johnson to clean, stable  │     (Model Convergence)  │         features for symmetry and linear convergence        │  └──────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┘                                 │                                 ▼  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │ Final Gate: `prism()` Report Certification                  │ ◄── GREEN LIGHT: "Model Ready"  │ Action: Verify Readiness >= 85 and 0 Veto Blockers          │  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

previous_headings: Recommended Remediation Order & Decision Hierarchy > Critical Decision: What If a Feature Has BOTH Instability (Drift) AND a Transformation Recommendation?
title: A Pre-Modeling Statistical Audit Framework
text: Rule 1: Never transform unstable feature blindly: drifting feature degrade production inference even scaled log-transformed. Rule 2: Attempt domain stabilization first: Can feature transformed stationary metric (e.g., computing percentage change, rolling z-scores, ratio--benchmark, seasonal differencing)? Rule 3: Drop non-stabilizable: drifting feature stabilized, drop model training set (heavily penalize via L1/L2 regularization). waste compute fitting Box-Cox parameters feature whose distribution moving time. Rule 4: Apply mathematical transforms last: engineered feature verified stable (PSI<0.10\text{PSI} < 0.10), apply recommended mathematical transformation (Log, Box-Cox, Yeo-Johnson) achieve normality enhance model convergence.

title: A Pre-Modeling Statistical Audit Framework
text: PrismR combines rigorous statistical methodology production-grade engineering: Core Innovation: Conceptualized, designed, implemented Model Readiness—automated statistical validation layer bridging gap raw data preprocessing machine learning model training. Distribution Diagnostics: Implemented higher-order sample moments (G1G_1 unbiased sample skewness, G2G_2 excess kurtosis) automated parameter bounds Box-Cox, Yeo-Johnson, Log transform recommendations. Covariate Drift: Engineered multi-vector distribution drift detection utilizing Population Stability Index (PSI) Bayesian Laplace smoothing 1D Wasserstein Distance (𝒲1\mathcal{W}_1) IQR scale-normalization. Leakage Detection: Built multi-stage leakage detection algorithms identifying surrogate identifiers (high-entropy/cardinality heuristics), duplicate feature hashes, bivariate Pearson correlations (|r|≥0.999|r| \ge 0.999). Decision Gatekeeping: Designed dual-layer scoring matrix combining 0–100 composite health score (0.40⋅Quality+0.45⋅Leakage+0.15⋅Transform0.40 \cdot \text{Quality} + 0.45 \cdot \text{Leakage} + 0.15 \cdot \text{Transform}) non-compensatory hard veto triggers (blocking models severe drift target leakers). Visualization Engineering: Developed 4 specialized ggplot2 diagnostic visualizations (radial macro gauge, circular diagnostic rose, bubble skewness map, radar dimensional profile). Built 99-test suite 100% test coverage via testthat. Configured GitHub Actions CI across 5-platform matrix (Ubuntu release/devel/oldrel, macOS release, Windows release) achieving 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 notes strict R CMD check ---cran. Automated documentation deployment pkgdown Bootstrap 5 hosted via GitHub Pages.

title: Feature Stability and Distribution Drift Assessment — feature_stability
text: list containing: stability_score Overall stability score 0 100. verdict Categorical stability verdict: "Stable", "Moderate Drift", "Unstable". variables data frame feature-level diagnostics containing variable, type, psi, wasserstein, stability_score, status. unstable_features Character vector features flagged severe drift (PSI >= 0.25). moderate_features Character vector features flagged moderate drift (0.10 <= PSI < 0.25). stable_features Character vector features exhibiting stable distributions (PSI < 0.10). method Character string describing assessment method used ("two_sample_comparison" "sequential_partition").

title: Feature Stability and Distribution Drift Assessment — feature_stability
text: Feature drift evaluated using standard industry thresholds: Stable (PSI < 0.10): Insignificant distributional shift. Moderate Drift (0.10 <= PSI < 0.25): Noticeable shift; monitoring recommended. Unstable / Severe Drift (PSI >= 0.25): Severe distributional divergence; retraining feature review required. categorical variables discrete bins, Bayesian Laplace smoothing applied prevent division--zero errors frequencies zero one partition. one dataset supplied, function performs sequential partition-based stability assessment (comparing first partition second partition observations). production monitoring, users provide reference current datasets separately via data current.

title: Feature Stability and Distribution Drift Assessment — feature_stability
code: # Single-dataset sequential drift evaluation res <- feature_stability(airquality) res$stability_score #> [1] 43.3 res$verdict #> [1] "Drift Warning (Unstable Features Detected)"  # Comparing reference baseline vs current dataset ref <- data.frame(val = rnorm(100, 0, 1)) cur <- data.frame(val = rnorm(100, 2, 1)) res2 <- feature_stability(ref, current = cur) res2$verdict #> [1] "Drift Warning (Unstable Features Detected)"

title: Perform Complete Prism Statistical Validation — prism
text: Evaluates dataset readiness predictive modeling across four foundational statistical pillars: data quality, data leakage, distribution transformations, feature stability. Produces overall Model Readiness score (0-100) gatekeeping verdict.

code: prism(data, target = NULL, current = NULL)

title: Perform Complete Prism Statistical Validation — prism
text: data data.frame assess. target Optional character string specifying name target/label variable. current Optional current data.frame evaluate distribution drift baseline data.

title: Perform Complete Prism Statistical Validation — prism
text: PrismReport S3 object containing: quality List data quality metrics returned quality_score. leakage List data leakage diagnostics returned detect_leakage. transformation List transformation recommendations returned recommend_transform. stability List stability metrics returned feature_stability. readiness Overall composite Model Readiness score (0-100). verdict Gatekeeping verdict: "Model Ready", "Proceed Caution", "Action Required".

title: Perform Complete Prism Statistical Validation — prism
text: four evaluation dimensions include: Data Quality: Evaluates missingness, duplicate rows, constant features. Data Leakage: Identifies identifier keys, duplicate features, high-cardinality columns, target correlation leakers. Transformations: Evaluates skewness excess kurtosis recommend variance-stabilizing transforms (Box-Cox, Yeo-Johnson, Log). Feature Stability: Assesses covariate distribution drift via Population Stability Index (PSI) Wasserstein distance.
